title: I built a game to help learn how to choose good interviewees
content:
Earlier this year I published the PEER technique for brainstorming interviewees: “four categories to help journalists generate more names on any given story — and think more creatively about whose voices might add something to that story.”

Now I’ve built a game to put that technique into practice — and improve your sourcing.

It’s much more fun.

Who should you call? has seven levels that move from identifying the type of source, to identifying who is missing from a story, to finding under-represented voices and picking a full interview list.

I included a ‘Blue vs Red’ teams mode for using the game in a class or training session. This allows you to introduce a competitive element by splitting a class into two teams. The lecturer can host a whole-class game on a big screen or let students play it themselves in smaller teams.

Play switches from one team to another when a team gets a question wrong. But play also switches if a team gets three answers correct in a row, to avoid the other team getting bored.

The game keeps track of each team’s scores and gives a running total at the end of each round.
